Handoff
Ask: which sorting algorithm does the fixture's `sort.rs` implement, and what is its worst case? Wanted: the algorithm and its worst-case complexity. For you: no edits made, and I did not run the full ulw-research team workflow because one file answers this. Now: done. Next: nothing.

`src/sort.rs` implements **quicksort with the Lomuto partition scheme**. It is in `/home/projects/ulwbench-home/tmp-new/ulw-bench-S6-r3-nTpcsT/src/sort.rs`, the current working directory.

- **Worst case: O(n²) time.** The pivot is always the last element (`arr[len - 1]`). On already-sorted or reverse-sorted input, every partition peels off only one element, so there are n levels of recursion with O(n) work each. The doc comment in the file says the same.
- **Average and best case: O(n log n).**
- **Space:** it sorts in place. The recursion stack is O(log n) on average but O(n) in the worst case, because it recurses on both halves without recursing on the smaller one first.
- **Stability:** it is not stable. The partition swaps non-adjacent elements.
- **Duplicates:** the `<=` comparison puts every element equal to the pivot on the left side. An all-equal array therefore also hits the O(n²) worst case.

I read only this one file, so the answer is about this fixture's implementation. I did not run it or look for tests.
